literal: Day jiachen: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On the jiachen day the court returned to the capital.

literal: Day guichou: an edict that General Who Conquers the West, Minister of Works, Prince of Shangdang Changsun Daosheng was to garrison Tongwan.
idiomatic: On the guichou day he ordered Changsun Daosheng, Prince of Shangdang, General Who Conquers the West and Minister of Works, to garrison Tongwan.

literal: Summer, fourth month, day yihai: Palace Attendant, Grand Preceptor, Prince of Yangping Du Chao was killed by his attendants.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the yihai day, Du Chao, Prince of Yangping, Palace Attendant and Grand Preceptor, was killed by his attendants.

literal: Fifth month, day dingyou: the imperial carriage traveled to the north of Yinshan.
idiomatic: On the dingyou day of the fifth month the emperor went north of Yinshan.

literal: Sixth month: northern tribesmen killed General Who Establishes Righteousness, Duke of Hengyang Mo Gu, and led more than five thousand households north in flight.
idiomatic: In the sixth month northern tribesmen killed Mo Gu, Duke of Hengyang, General Who Establishes Righteousness, and led more than five thousand households north.

literal: They were pursued in the southern desert; their chieftains were killed and the remainder were moved to Ji, Xiang, and Ding provinces as camp households.
idiomatic: Pursued in the southern desert, their chiefs were killed and the rest were settled in Ji, Xiang, and Ding as camp households.

literal: Prince of Xiping Tuyuhun Muli Yan killed his nephew Weidai.
idiomatic: Muli Yan, Prince of Xiping of the Tuyuhun, killed his nephew Weidai.

literal: That month Weidai's younger brother Chiliyan and others came in flight and begged troops.
idiomatic: That month Chiliyan, Weidai's younger brother, and others fled in and begged for troops.

literal: Chiliyan was made Prince Who Returns to Righteousness.
idiomatic: Chiliyan was made Prince Who Returns to Righteousness.

literal: Autumn, seventh month, day guimao: Juqu Bing, Inspector of Eastern Yongzhou, plotted rebellion and was executed in secret.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the guimao day, Juqu Bing, Inspector of Eastern Yongzhou, plotted rebellion and was secretly executed.

literal: Eighth month, day yichou: a hunt was held in Hexi.
idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the yichou day, a hunt was held in Hexi.

literal: Day renwu: an edict that Supernumerary Palace Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Gao Ji was to go as envoy to Liu Yilong.
idiomatic: On the renwu day he ordered Gao Ji, Supernumerary Palace Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, as envoy to Liu Yilong.

literal: Prince of Jin Fulu commanded the armies of Gaoping and Liangzhou against Tuyuhun Muli Yan.
idiomatic: Fulu, Prince of Jin, commanded the armies of Gaoping and Liangzhou against Muli Yan of the Tuyuhun.

literal: Ninth month: the Emperor came from Hexi to Mayi and reviewed troops at Guochuan.
idiomatic: In the ninth month the Emperor came from Hexi to Mayi and reviewed troops at Guochuan.

literal: Day jihai: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On the jihai day the court returned to the capital.

literal: Day dingwei: the imperial carriage traveled to the southern desert.
idiomatic: On the dingwei day the emperor went to the southern desert.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day guiwei: Prince of Jin Fulu greatly defeated Muli Yan; Muli Yan fled to Bailan.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the guiwei day, Fulu routed Muli Yan, who fled to Bailan.

literal: Muli Yan's younger cousin Funian, Chief Clerk Hejiuli, and the great chieftain E led more than thirteen thousand households of their tribe to submit inward.
idiomatic: Funian, Muli Yan's younger cousin, Chief Clerk Hejiuli, and the great chieftain E led more than thirteen thousand households to submit.

literal: Eleventh month: Liu Yilong sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month Liu Yilong sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Twelfth month: the state of Sute sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month the state of Sute sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Day bingxu: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On the bingxu day the court returned to the capital.

literal: Year 6, spring, first month, day xinhai: the imperial carriage traveled to Dingzhou, summoned the elders, and inquired after them.
idiomatic: In the sixth year, on the xinhai day of the first month of spring, the emperor went to Dingzhou, summoned the elders, and inquired after them.

literal: An edict that Concurrent Supernumerary Palace Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Song Yin was to go as envoy to Liu Yilong.
idiomatic: He ordered Song Yin, Concurrent Supernumerary Palace Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, as envoy to Liu Yilong.

literal: Second month: he then traveled west to Shangdang and viewed an intertwined tree at Xuanshi.
idiomatic: In the second month he went west to Shangdang and viewed an intertwined tree at Xuanshi.

literal: West to Tujing: rebellious Hu who had been moved were punished and assigned out to commanderies and districts.
idiomatic: West to Tujing: moved rebels were punished and assigned to commanderies and districts.

literal: Third month, day gengshen: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: In the third month, on the gengshen day, the court returned to the capital.

literal: An edict that all doubtful criminal cases were to be sent to the Secretariat and decided by canonical principle.
idiomatic: He ordered that all doubtful criminal cases go to the Secretariat and be decided by canonical principle.

literal: That month Duke of Jiuquan Hao Wen rebelled at Xingcheng and killed the defending general Wang Fan.
idiomatic: That month Hao Wen, Duke of Jiuquan, rebelled at Xingcheng and killed the garrison commander Wang Fan.

literal: District clerk Gai Xian led his clan to attack Wen; Wen abandoned the city and fled, killed himself, and his household was executed.
idiomatic: District clerk Gai Xian led his clan against Wen; Wen fled, killed himself, and his household was executed.

literal: Summer, fourth month, day gengxu: General Who Conquers the West, Prince of Gaoliang Na and others campaigned against Tuyuhun Muli Yan at Yinping Bailan.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the gengxu day, Na, Prince of Gaoliang, General Who Conquers the West, and others campaigned against Muli Yan at Yinping Bailan.

literal: An edict that Inspector of Qinzhou, Duke of Tianshui Feng Jiwen, was to strike Muli Yan's nephew Shigui at Fuhan, and Palace Attendant, Duke of Chenggong Wandu Gui was to rush troops west from Liangzhou to raid Shanshan.
idiomatic: He ordered Feng Jiwen, Duke of Tianshui, Inspector of Qinzhou, against Shigui at Fuhan, and Wandu Gui, Duke of Chenggong, Palace Attendant, to rush troops from Liangzhou west against Shanshan.

literal: Sixth month, day renchen: the imperial carriage toured north.
idiomatic: On the renchen day of the sixth month the emperor toured north.

literal: Shigui, hearing the army was coming, abandoned the city and fled by night.
idiomatic: Hearing the army was coming, Shigui abandoned the city and fled by night.

literal: Autumn, eighth month, day dinghai: Feng Jiwen entered Fuhan and moved a thousand households back to Shanggui.
idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn, on the dinghai day, Feng Jiwen entered Fuhan and moved a thousand households back to Shanggui.

literal: Day renchen: Wandu Gui with light horse reached Shanshan, seized its king Zhenda, and sent him to the capital; the Emperor was greatly pleased and treated him generously.
idiomatic: On the renchen day Wandu Gui reached Shanshan with light horse, seized King Zhenda, and sent him to the capital; the Emperor was greatly pleased and treated him generously.

literal: The imperial carriage traveled to the north of Yinshan and halted at the Broad Virtue Palace.
idiomatic: The emperor went north of Yinshan and halted at Broad Virtue Palace.

literal: An edict mobilized troops throughout the realm, one man in three, each to stand in readiness awaiting further orders.
idiomatic: He mobilized troops throughout the realm, one man in three, each to stand ready for orders.

literal: More than five thousand households of various mixed peoples were moved to the northern frontier.
idiomatic: More than five thousand households of mixed peoples were moved to the northern frontier.

literal: The people were ordered to move north to pasture livestock as far as the broad desert, to bait the Rouran.
idiomatic: The people were ordered north to pasture as far as the broad desert to bait the Rouran.

literal: Day renyin: Prince of Gaoliang Na's army reached Mantoucheng; Muli Yan drove his tribes west across the shifting sands and Na pursued urgently.
idiomatic: On the renyin day Na's army reached Mantoucheng; Muli Yan drove his tribes west across the sands and Na pursued hard.

literal: The former Western Qin king Murong Kui's heir prince Beinang resisted the army in battle; Na defeated him; Beinang fled with light horse; Duke of Zhongshan Du Feng with picked horse pursued across Sanwei to Snow Mountain, captured Beinang and Shigui alive, and Qifu Chipan's son Chenglong, and sent them to the capital.
idiomatic: Beinang, heir of the former Western Qin king Murong Kui, resisted; Na defeated him; Beinang fled; Du Feng, Duke of Zhongshan, pursued with picked horse across Sanwei to Snow Mountain and took Beinang, Shigui, and Chenglong, son of Qifu Chipan, alive to the capital.

literal: Muli Yan then went west into the state of Khotan.
idiomatic: Muli Yan then went west into Khotan.

literal: Ninth month: the Lushui Hu Gai Wu gathered a host and rebelled at Xingcheng.
idiomatic: In the ninth month Gai Wu of the Lushui Hu gathered a host and rebelled at Xingcheng.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day wuzi: Deputy garrison commander of Chang'an Yuan He led troops against him and was killed by Wu.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the wuzi day, Yuan He, deputy commander of Chang'an, led troops against him and was killed by Wu.

literal: Wu's party then flourished; the people all crossed the Wei and fled to the southern mountains.
idiomatic: Wu's party then grew strong; the people crossed the Wei and fled to the southern mountains.

literal: Thereupon an edict mobilized Gaoping Tiele horse for Chang'an, and ordered General Shusun Ba by rapid relay to take command of Bing, Qin, and Yong troops and encamp north of the Wei.
idiomatic: He mobilized Gaoping Tiele horse for Chang'an and ordered Shusun Ba by rapid relay to command Bing, Qin, and Yong troops north of the Wei.

literal: Eleventh month: Prince of Gaoliang Na led the army back to the capital.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month Na led the army back to the capital.

literal: Day jiwei: Na and Palace Attendant, Duke of Anding Han Mao were sent with horse to encamp in Yangping commandery of Xiangzhou; people of Jizhou were levied to build a pontoon bridge at Que'ao Ford.
idiomatic: On the jiwei day Na and Han Mao, Duke of Anding, Palace Attendant, were sent with horse to Yangping in Xiangzhou; people of Jizhou built a pontoon at Que'ao Ford.

literal: Gai Wu sent his tribal chief Bai Guangping west to raid Xinping; chieftains of the various Yi of Anding all gathered hosts in response and killed the garrison commander of Qian city.
idiomatic: Gai Wu sent Bai Guangping west to raid Xinping; Anding chieftains rose in response and killed the commander of Qian city.

literal: Wu then advanced to Li Run Fort and divided troops to raid Linjin and Bayi.
idiomatic: Wu advanced to Li Run Fort and sent columns to raid Linjin and Bayi.

literal: [3] General Zhang Zhi fought him and greatly defeated him; more than thirty thousand soldiers drowned in the river.
idiomatic: General Zhang Zhi fought him, [3] routed him, and more than thirty thousand drowned in the river.

literal: Wu again sent troops west to raid as far as Chang'an; General Shusun Ba fought him north of the Wei, [4] greatly defeated him, and beheaded more than thirty thousand.
idiomatic: Wu again sent troops toward Chang'an; Shusun Ba fought him north of the Wei, [4] routed him, and beheaded more than thirty thousand.

literal: Day gengshen: Prince of Liaodong Dou Loutou died.
idiomatic: On the gengshen day Dou Loutou, Prince of Liaodong, died.

literal: Shu of Hedong, Xue Yongzong, gathered a band, stole several thousand government horses, drove more than three thousand men into the Fen bend, and linked with Gai Wu in the west, receiving offices and titles from him.
idiomatic: Xue Yongzong of Hedong Shu gathered a band, stole thousands of government horses, drove more than three thousand into the Fen bend, and joined Gai Wu in the west, taking rank from him.

literal: Inspector of Qinzhou, Duke of Jincheng Zhou Luguan led troops against him but could not overcome him and returned.
idiomatic: Zhou Luguan, Duke of Jincheng, Inspector of Qinzhou, attacked him but failed and returned.

literal: Day gengwu: an edict that Palace Attendant, Duke of Fufeng Yuan Chuzhen and Minister of Works, Duke of Pingyang Murong Song, with twenty thousand horse, were to campaign against Xue Yongzong;
idiomatic: On the gengwu day he ordered Yuan Chuzhen, Duke of Fufeng, Palace Attendant, and Murong Song, Duke of Pingyang, Minister of Works, with twenty thousand horse against Xue Yongzong;

literal: an edict that Palace Attendant Yiba with five generals and thirty thousand horse was to campaign against Gai Wu; Duke of Xiping Kou Ti with three generals and ten thousand horse was to campaign against Wu's partisan Bai Guangping.
idiomatic: he ordered Yiba, Palace Attendant, with five generals and thirty thousand horse against Gai Wu; and Kou Ti, Duke of Xiping, with three generals and ten thousand horse against Bai Guangping.

literal: Gai Wu styled himself King of Heavenly Terrace and appointed the hundred offices.
idiomatic: Gai Wu styled himself King of Heavenly Terrace and set up the hundred offices.

literal: Day xinwei: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On the xinwei day the court returned to the capital.

literal: Brave men from six provinces, twenty thousand in number, were selected; Prince of Yongchang Ren and Prince of Gaoliang Na were each to command one route of ten thousand horse and raid south of the Huai and Si, moving the people of Qing and Xu to fill Hebei.
idiomatic: Twenty thousand brave men from six provinces were chosen; Ren, Prince of Yongchang, and Na, Prince of Gaoliang, each led ten thousand horse south of the Huai and Si and moved Qing and Xu people to fill Hebei.

literal: Day guimao: the imperial carriage toured west.
idiomatic: On the guimao day the emperor toured west.

literal: Year 7, spring, first month, day wuchen: the imperial carriage halted at Eastern Yongzhou.
idiomatic: In the seventh year, on the wuchen day of the first month of spring, the court halted at Eastern Yongzhou.

literal: Day gengwu: Xue Yongzong's fortified camp was besieged.
idiomatic: On the gengwu day Yongzong's camp was besieged.

literal: Yongzong came out to fight and was greatly defeated; the six armies pressed him and his host collapsed.
idiomatic: Yongzong came out to fight, was routed, and the six armies overran his host.

literal: Men and women of Yongzong's party, young and old alike, threw themselves into the Fen and died.
idiomatic: Yongzong's people, young and old, threw themselves into the Fen and died.

literal: Day xinwei: the imperial carriage traveled south to Fenyin.
idiomatic: On the xinwei day the emperor went south to Fenyin.

literal: Day gengchen: the Emperor came to Xishui.
idiomatic: On the gengchen day the Emperor came to Xishui.

literal: Gai Wu withdrew to Beidi.
idiomatic: Gai Wu withdrew to Beidi.

literal: Second month, day bingxu: he came to Chang'an and inquired after the elders.
idiomatic: In the second month, on the bingxu day, he came to Chang'an and inquired after the elders.

literal: Day dinghai: he came to Kunming Pool.
idiomatic: On the dinghai day he came to Kunming Pool.

literal: Day bingshen: he came to Zhouzhi and executed the rebel people Geng Qing and Sun Wen at two forts for communicating with Gai Wu.
idiomatic: On the bingshen day he came to Zhouzhi and executed Geng Qing and Sun Wen at two forts for plotting with Gai Wu.

literal: The army halted at Chencang and executed the Di of Sanguan who had harmed the garrison commander.
idiomatic: The army halted at Chencang and executed the Di of Sanguan who had killed the garrison commander.

literal: Returning, he came to Yong city and hunted on the south of Mount Qi.
idiomatic: Returning, he came to Yong and hunted south of Mount Qi.

literal: On the northern route Yiba and others greatly defeated Gai Wu at Xingcheng; Wu abandoned his horses and fled.
idiomatic: Yiba and the northern army routed Gai Wu at Xingcheng; Wu abandoned his horses and fled.

literal: Prince of Yongchang Ren reached Gaoping, captured Liu Yilong's general Wang Zhang, raided Jinxiang and Fangyu, and moved five thousand households to Hebei.
idiomatic: Ren reached Gaoping, took Liu Yilong's general Wang Zhang, raided Jinxiang and Fangyu, and moved five thousand households to Hebei.

literal: Prince of Gaoliang Na reached Dongpingling east of Jinan and moved more than six thousand households to Hebei.
idiomatic: Na reached Dongpingling east of Jinan and moved more than six thousand households to Hebei.

literal: Third month: an edict that all provinces were to bury Buddhist monks alive and destroy all Buddha images.
idiomatic: In the third month he ordered all provinces to bury monks alive and destroy Buddha images.

literal: Two thousand families of artisans of Chang'an were moved to the capital.
idiomatic: Two thousand artisan families of Chang'an were moved to the capital.

literal: The imperial carriage turned back, came to the Luo River, and divided the army to execute the rebel Qiang of Li Run.
idiomatic: The court turned back to the Luo and sent columns to execute the rebel Qiang of Li Run.

literal: That month Bian of Jincheng frontier and Liang Hui of Tianshui rebelled and held the eastern city of Shanggui.
idiomatic: That month Bian of the Jincheng frontier and Liang Hui of Tianshui rebelled and held the eastern city of Shanggui.

literal: Inspector of Qinzhou Feng Jiwen attacked them, beheaded Bian, and the host again set up Hui as leader.
idiomatic: Feng Jiwen attacked, beheaded Bian, and the host again made Hui leader.

literal: Summer, fourth month, day jiashen: the imperial carriage returned from Chang'an.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the jiashen day, the court returned from Chang'an.

literal: Day wuzi: the five-story Buddha tower of Ye was destroyed; two jade seals were found in the clay images, both reading "Receiving the mandate from Heaven, long life and eternal stability," and one carved at the side: "The seal of Han transmitted to Wei."
idiomatic: On the wuzi day Ye's five-story Buddha tower was torn down; two jade seals were found in the clay images reading "Receiving the mandate from Heaven, long life and eternal stability," one side carved "The seal Han transmitted to Wei."

literal: Fifth month, day guihai: Duke of Anfeng Yan Gen led horse to Shanggui and with Jiwen campaigned against Liang Hui; Hui fled to Hanzhong.
idiomatic: On the guihai day of the fifth month Yan Gen, Duke of Anfeng, led horse to Shanggui and with Jiwen attacked Liang Hui; Hui fled to Hanzhong.

literal: Gai Wu again gathered at Xingcheng, styled himself King of Qin and Earth, and by provisional appointment drew the mountain people; his host revived.
idiomatic: Gai Wu again gathered at Xingcheng, styled himself King of Qin and Earth, appointed mountain people, and his host revived.

literal: Thereupon Ren and Na were sent to command the armies of the northern route together against him.
idiomatic: Ren and Na were sent to command the northern armies together against him.

literal: Sixth month, day jiashen: troops of Ding, Ji, and Xiang provinces, twenty thousand men, were mobilized to encamp in the valleys of the southern mountains of Chang'an to prevent escape.
idiomatic: On the jiashen day of the sixth month twenty thousand men of Ding, Ji, and Xiang were posted in the southern valleys of Chang'an to block escape.

literal: Day bingxu: troops of Si, You, Ding, and Ji provinces, one hundred thousand men, were mobilized to build the encircling barrier of the capital frontier, from Shanggu west to the Yellow River, a thousand li in breadth and length alike.
idiomatic: On the bingxu day one hundred thousand men of Si, You, Ding, and Ji built the capital frontier barrier from Shanggu west to the Yellow River, a thousand li each way.

literal: Autumn, eighth month: Gai Wu was killed by his subordinates; his head was sent to the capital.
idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn Gai Wu was killed by his men; his head was sent to the capital.

literal: Prince of Yongchang Ren pacified his embers.
idiomatic: Ren, Prince of Yongchang, pacified his embers.

literal: Prince of Gaoliang Na defeated Gai Wu's partisan Bai Guangping;
idiomatic: Na defeated Bai Guangping, Gai Wu's partisan;

literal: Tuluona of Tulu Road was captured alive in Anding and beheaded in the capital.
idiomatic: Tuluona of Tulu Road was taken alive in Anding and beheaded in the capital.

literal: Duke of Lueyang Jie'er's princely rank was restored.
idiomatic: Jie'er, Duke of Lueyang, had his princely rank restored.

literal: Year 8, spring, first month: the Hu of Tujing blocked the passes and acted as bandits.
idiomatic: In the eighth year, first month of spring, the Hu of Tujing blocked the passes and turned bandit.

literal: An edict that General Who Conquers the East, Prince of Wuchang Ti, and General Who Conquers the South, Prince of Huainan Ta, were to campaign against them but could not overcome them.
idiomatic: He ordered Ti, Prince of Wuchang, General Who Conquers the East, and Ta, Prince of Huainan, General Who Conquers the South, against them but they could not take them.

literal: The mountain Hu Cao Puhun and others crossed west of the river, held the mountains to secure themselves, and drew the various Hu of Shuofang.
idiomatic: Cao Puhun and other mountain Hu crossed west of the river, held the mountains, and drew the Hu of Shuofang.

literal: Ti and others led the army against Puhun.
idiomatic: Ti and others led the army against Puhun.

literal: Second month, day jimao: Na and others from Anding campaigned against and pacified the Shuofang Hu, then joined Ti and others to attack Puhun together, beheaded him, and those of his host who fled to the passes and died numbered in the tens of thousands.
idiomatic: On the jimao day of the second month Na from Anding pacified the Shuofang Hu, joined Ti, and together attacked Puhun, beheaded him, and tens of thousands died fleeing to the passes.

literal: Day guimao: the imperial carriage traveled to Zhongshan and distributed rewards to the accompanying civil and military officers, each according to rank.
idiomatic: On the guimao day the emperor went to Zhongshan and rewarded the accompanying officers, each by rank.

literal: The people of Yiyi in Gaoyang did not obey the government command; they were punished and pacified, and the remainder were moved to Beidi.
idiomatic: The people of Yiyi in Gaoyang disobeyed; they were punished and pacified, and the remainder were moved to Beidi.
